reason: The complete batch review found page-local, repairable proof, domain, and sign defects. The prerequisite issues can be resolved rigorously on the assigned pages; no immediate owner escalation is required.

findings.reason: Step 1.2 bounds the product of resolvent and B using cor-operator-norm-submultiplicative-and-t-star-t-identity, whose statement is limited to finite-dimensional spaces, while H may be infinite-dimensional. Cite the general bounded-operator composition inequality or prove the estimate locally.

Step 1.2 swaps the coefficients of the parallel and perpendicular components in qvq^{-1}. For q=c+sr and v=αr+w with w⊥r, the coefficients are (c²+s²)αr and (c²−s²)w; correct them to support the stated rotation identity.

Facts [F2] and step 2.1 rely on lem-nrqm-symmetries-spatial-rotation-action claiming individual Q_j and P_k domains are rotation invariant; this is false when a rotation mixes coordinates. Also define the domains of the rotated sums explicitly. Use maximal directional multiplier and derivative domains and prove the conjugations on them.

Step 1.1 applies the cited flow-commutation result, which assumes a bounded self-adjoint operator, to arbitrary fibre matrices M_s(A_i(t)), generally non-self-adjoint. The cited SU2 clause (d) is a scope clause. Prove the required commutation for these matrices, for example by componentwise factorization or self-adjoint real and imaginary parts.

Step 1.1 calls the squared total-spin components commuting self-adjoint summands. They need not commute. Self-adjointness of their sum follows because each square is self-adjoint; cite the tensor-spin supplier for the Casimir commutation.

With the stated linear-first inner product and Pauli σ_y, ⟨σ_yv,v⟩=−2 Im(v₁ overline{v₂}); the Example uses the opposite sign. Correct the Bloch-vector y component and its angular parametrization; the general directional probabilities are otherwise wrong when n has a y component.
The Example applies the sphere operator L₃ to the polynomial h₁ₘ on ℝ³. State the eigenvalue for Y₁ₘ=h₁ₘ|S², or give the corresponding polynomial generator identity separately.

Clause (i) applies H_Z and gives its expectation for every unit f∈L², although H₀f and ⟨H₀⟩ are not defined for a general such f. Require f∈D(H₀) for these claims, or separate them from the flow identity that holds on all L² states.

Step 3.1 drops the sector weights when integrating the unnormalized momentum expectations. Their increments are ±γħGτw_±/2; divide by w_± to obtain the normalized sector means, and sum the unnormalized increments for the total mean.
